newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Top Colombia lawman to announce presidential bid.
newsitem.headline: Top Colombia lawman to announce presidential bid.

text.p: Colombia's Chief Prosecutor, Alfonso Valdivieso, will resign later this week or early next week to prepare a bid for the presidency in 1998, sources close to Valdivieso said Monday.
Valdivieso, a fervent anti-drug crusader, appeared likely to become the most popular potential candidate among voters for the presidential race, according to recent polls.

"The chief prosecutor has already made his decision and it is possible that at the end of the this week or next week at the latest he will resign to launch his candidacy for the presidency," a source close to Valdivieso said.
Valdivieso was appointed in 1994, less than two weeks after President Ernesto Samper took office.

He made his mark heading the so-called 8,000 Process, an investigation into high-level political corruption, including allegations that Samper financed his election campaign with millions of dollars in donations from the Cali drug cartel.
Valdivieso, a member of the ruling Liberal Party, is widely seen as an ally of former president Cesar Gaviria, currently head of the Organisation of American States (OAS).

A survey published in the latest edition of the respected Cambio 16 political magazine found 58 percent of 600 voters questioned would vote for Valdivieso while 26 percent said they would vote for Interior Minister Horacio Serpa, Samper's right-hand man. No margin of error was stated.
Former Bogota mayor Antanas Mockus and a former Colombian ambassador to the United States, Carlos Lleras de la Fuente, have also signalled they intend to run.
